title: A chance pleasure without holding its promise

captions.energy: Clinging to a promised pleasant continuation

meaning: Permission to release continuation supports leisure together when a strong promise of pleasure meets an abrupt change of circumstances.
text: An unplanned pleasure can quickly acquire too large a promise. The Wheel of Fortune in the physical position of Svadhisthana helps adapt leisure and use an opening. The Devil in energy holds its pleasant continuation as something difficult to release. The Tower in emotions makes broken expectation feel sharp. Ordinary unavailability can then seem to cost the whole evening. Both benefit from distinguishing the pleasant moment that happened from the promise added to it: the first already belonged to your experience, while the second need not necessarily be fulfilled.

Suppose you unexpectedly find an interesting street performance and decide to stay for the next act. The programme then ends abruptly. **Pleasure already shared keeps its value without a promised continuation.** You can acknowledge frustration and choose the remaining time. Anticipation need not remove enjoyment of the first act. Being together permits another turn even if brightness does not immediately return and simply sitting quietly now appeals.

The difficulty is seeking an equally intense replacement at once. You hurry to another stage, debate alternatives and move further from actual desire. An external obstacle continues through tension between you. Flexibility helps when it permits lost expectation without blame. Chance leisure owes no uninterrupted chain of rewards to remain a good shared memory you can preserve and finish without proving its value again.
